source: 2026 Prayer Calendar for the Diocese of Idaho
sourceFile: "2026 Prayer Calendar for the Diocese of Idaho.xlsx", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 1xMZWFpVrKnHqPWYkmrttFn9koK9vt9vR, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer"); original diocesan source per Josh's own roster (a live Google Sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1fJVztvWOsW_aAT4hsjY92njRCJY67al2yWxujznO7ww/edit
notes: The diocese's own full name is not printed within the spreadsheet's body (it refers to itself only as 'our Diocese', 'our Bishop', etc.); 'Diocese of Idaho' is taken from Josh's own filename for this document, not fabricated, but disclosed here as coming from the filename rather than the document's own printed text.

The source has a fourth 'Anglican Communion Prayer Cycle' column reproducing the worldwide Anglican Communion Cycle of Prayer's province name for that week -- deliberately NOT transcribed into this file's `entries`, since that content is the separate, already-ingested scope-'communion' corpus (anglican-communion-2026.json), matching the same decision made for episcopal-connecticut-2026.json.

The source's third column, a weekly Social Justice intercession theme, IS included here as a `category` subject per week (not a named group/congregation in the usual sense of this schema's `category` type, but the diocese's own stated second half of its weekly cycle of prayer, disclosed as such rather than silently dropped).

CORRECTED, not preserved as printed: the source prints four consecutive weeks as 'Sunday, June 5 Proper 9', 'Sunday, June 12 Proper 10', 'Sunday, June 19 Proper 11', and 'Sunday, June 26 Proper 12' -- immediately AFTER an already-printed 'Sunday, June 28 Proper 8' and immediately BEFORE 'Sunday, August 2 Proper 13'. None of June 5/12/19/26, 2026 are Sundays (verified directly: Sunday, January 4, 2026, the source's own first date, is exactly 21 weeks before June 28 and 26 weeks before July 5, confirming July 5/12/19/26 are the real Sundays, not June); the Proper-number sequence (8, then 9-10-11-12, then 13) is otherwise perfectly consistent with the surrounding weeks and only resolves if these four are July, not June. This is a source-side labeling error (most likely an entire block mislabeled by one month), not an ambiguous name -- corrected to July 5/12/19/26 per this project's own standing rule that a verifiably wrong date is fixed, not merely flagged (the same rule already applied to EOR/OOR sanctoral dates elsewhere in this corpus). If Josh's own copy of this spreadsheet is later revised to read 'July' directly, this file will already match it.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Second Sunday of Christmas

subjects.name: Redeemer Episcopal Church
For a new year shaped by justice: that every community may have safe housing, food, and hope.

entries.liturgicalNote: The First Sunday after the Epiphany: The Baptism of Our Lord

subjects.name: St. David's Episcopal Church
For survivors of human trafficking and exploitation, and for courageous action to protect the vulnerable and prosecute abuse.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Second Sunday after the Epiphany

subjects.name: Grace Episcopal Church
For racial justice and reconciliation—especially where systems harm Black, Indigenous, and people of color—and for hearts brave enough to change.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Third Sunday after the Epiphany

subjects.name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church
For unity across divides: among Christian traditions and with our neighbors of other faiths, that we may seek the common good together.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fourth Sunday after the Epiphany

subjects.name: St. Matthew's Episcopal Church
For those living in poverty and without stable housing, and for policies and neighbors that make dignity affordable and real.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fifth Sunday after the Epiphany

subjects.name: St. Paul's Episcopal Church
For equitable healthcare and mental health support, so no one is denied care because of cost, stigma, or geography.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Last Sunday after the Epiphany

subjects.name: Paradise Point Camp
For workers: fair wages, safe workplaces, and the right to organize, especially for those in low-paid and invisible labor.

entries.liturgicalNote: The First Sunday in Lent

subjects.name: Trinity Episcopal Church
For those impacted by mass incarceration, and for restorative justice that heals victims, repairs harm, and offers true paths home.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Second Sunday in Lent

subjects.name: St. Thomas Episcopal Church
For migrants and refugees on the move, that borders may be met with mercy, and families may be protected and reunited.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Third Sunday in Lent

subjects.name: St. Mary's Episcopal Church
For women and girls worldwide: safety from violence, equal opportunity, and voices honored in every home and workplace.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fourth Sunday in Lent

subjects.name: St. James Episcopal Church
For people living with disabilities, that communities remove barriers and build belonging, access, and respect.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fifth Sunday in Lent

subjects.name: St. Andrew's Episcopal Church
For clean and affordable water for all, and for wise stewardship where scarcity, pollution, and inequity threaten life.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Sunday of the Passion: Palm Sunday

subjects.name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church
For those facing hunger and food insecurity, and for fair systems that support farmers, workers, and nutritious food for every table.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Sunday of the Resurrection: Easter Day

subjects.name: Christ Episcopal Church
For peace in places of war and unrest, for protection of civilians, and for leaders willing to choose diplomacy over domination.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Second Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: All Saints Episcopal Church
For climate action rooted in justice—so that those least responsible are no longer forced to bear the greatest burdens.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Third Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church
For Indigenous peoples: protection of land and language, honoring of treaties, and healing from historic and ongoing harms.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fourth Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: The Ministry of our Bishop, the Rt. Rev. Jos Tharakan
For education equity, that every child—regardless of zip code—has excellent schools, supportive teachers, and safe learning spaces.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fifth Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church
For children in vulnerable situations—foster care, detention, or unstable homes—and for adults who will advocate fiercely for them.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Sixth Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: Church of The Ascension
For caregivers and parents, especially those raising children with limited resources, that they receive support, rest, and respect.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Seventh Sunday of Easter

subjects.name: The Staff of our Diocesan Office in Boise
For the dignity and safety of LGBTQ+ people, that bullying and violence end, and that every person may flourish without fear.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Day of Pentecost: Whitsunday

subjects.name: St. Stephen's Episcopal Church
For communities scarred by gun violence, and for courageous peacemaking that reduces harm and protects life.

entries.liturgicalNote: The First Sunday after Pentecost: Trinity Sunday

subjects.name: Good Shepherd Episcopal Church
For compassionate responses to addiction: prevention, treatment, recovery support, and an end to shame that isolates.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 5: The Second Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Michael's Cathedral
For people persecuted for their faith or identity, and for the freedom to worship, speak, and live without violence.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 6: The Third Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Holy Nativity Episcopal Church
For integrity in public life: truthful speech, fair elections, and civic courage that resists corruption and dehumanization.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 7: The Fourth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Grace Episcopal Church
For refugees and displaced people rebuilding after conflict and disaster, and for welcoming communities that share resources generously.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 8: The Fifth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Trinity Episcopal Church
For oceans, rivers, and coasts, and for environmental justice where pollution and extraction endanger the poor first.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 9: The Sixth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Epiphany Episcopal Church
For freedom that includes everyone: that patriotism becomes care for neighbors, and that rights are matched by responsibility.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 10: The Seventh Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Calvary Episcopal Church
For those returning from prison and detention, that communities offer work, housing, mentoring, and mercy instead of rejection.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 11: The Eighth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Francis of the Tetons
For elders and those who are isolated, that loneliness be met with friendship, accessible care, and intergenerational community.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 12: The Ninth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Redeemer Episcopal Church
For communities facing extreme heat, storms, and wildfire, especially those without resources to recover, and for resilient, just rebuilding.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 13: The Tenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. David's Episcopal Church
For families separated by immigration systems, and for humane pathways that honor safety, work, and belonging.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 14: The Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Grace Episcopal Church
For nonviolent peacemakers—teachers, organizers, and neighbors—who interrupt hatred and model brave, practical compassion.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 15: The Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church
For economic justice: relief from crushing debt, fair taxation, and systems that reward work without exploiting workers.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 16: The Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Matthew's Episcopal Church
For students and educators as a new school season approaches, that learning be safe, inclusive, and supported with adequate resources.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 17: The Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Paul's Episcopal Church
For laborers and job seekers, especially those underpaid or unemployed, that dignified work and just benefits be available to all.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 18: The Fifteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Trinity Episcopal Church
For the healing of creation: that our churches and households reduce waste, conserve energy, and protect the earth we share.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 19: The Sixteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: The Committees and Commissions of our Diocese
For fair trade and ethical supply chains, that farmers and workers receive just compensation and safe conditions.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 20: The Seventeenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Thomas Episcopal Church
For peacebuilding in our neighborhoods and nations, that conflicts be handled without violence and with a commitment to human dignity.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 21: The Eighteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Mary's Episcopal Church
For those sleeping outside or in unstable housing, and for affordable homes, supportive services, and communities that refuse to look away.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 22: The Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. James Episcopal Church
For care of animals and the web of life, and for stewardship that rejects cruelty and protects habitats for future generations.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 23: The Twentieth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Andrew's Episcopal Church
For Indigenous communities today: for cultural renewal, land protection, and justice for missing and murdered Indigenous people.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 24: The Twenty-First Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: St. Luke's Episcopal Church
For food justice worldwide, that harvests be shared fairly, hunger ends, and farmers are protected from exploitation and climate shocks.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 25: The Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Christ Episcopal Church
For survivors of domestic violence and coercive control, and for safe shelters, legal protection, and healing that lasts.

entries.liturgicalNote: All Saints

subjects.name: All Saints Episcopal Church
For those we remember who died through violence, neglect, or injustice, and for the living who carry grief and trauma.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 27: The Twenty-Fourth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church
For humane immigration reform, an end to dehumanizing rhetoric, and practical welcome rooted in solidarity.

entries.liturgicalNote: Proper 28: The Twenty-Fifth Sunday after Pentecost

subjects.name: The Ministry of our Archdeacon, the Ven. Eileen O'Shea
For climate and environmental justice in the decisions of nations and corporations, that profit never outweighs human life.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Last Sunday after Pentecost: Christ the King

subjects.name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church
For an end to violence against women and gender-based violence everywhere, and for cultures that honor consent and equality.

entries.liturgicalNote: The First Sunday of Advent

subjects.name: Church of The Ascension
For Advent hope that is active: that we prepare room through generosity, advocacy, and attention to those pushed to the margins.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Second Sunday of Advent

subjects.name: St. Stephen's Episcopal Church
For global peace and disarmament, that resources be turned from weapons toward health, education, and human flourishing.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Third Sunday of Advent

subjects.name: Good Shepherd Episcopal Church
For an end to antisemitism, Islamophobia, and every form of religious hatred, and for communities that protect one another with courage.

entries.liturgicalNote: The Fourth Sunday of Advent

subjects.name: St. Michael's Cathedral
For those displaced or homeless during the holidays, that they find warmth, community, and pathways to stable, dignified living.

entries.liturgicalNote: The First Sunday after Christmas

subjects.name: Holy Nativity Episcopal Church
We pray in gratitude for the year’s lessons, and we commit ourselves anew to justice, mercy, and humble walking with God and neighbor.
